$comment: WHAT SHAPE THE REPOSITORY ROOT AND agent/ ARE ALLOWED TO HAVE.
WHY IT IS DATA AND NOT CODE. Two defects in one week showed that both trees
were clean by luck rather than by rule. Debris (`aa.jsonl`, `zz.jsonl`,
`.events.jsonl`, `.lastevent-*.json`, `.requests`, `.local/`, `claude/`) sat
untracked at the repository root, written by the old bash worklist suites; and
a second reggate ledger appeared under `.claude/hooks/stop/agent/` because
`wl_reggate.debt_dir()` fell back to a cwd-relative root. Neither was a bug in
one script. Both were a missing rule about where a file may be.
THIS FILE IS THE RULE. `.ci/rediacc_ci/quality/tree_shape.py` reads it and
nothing else: every permitted name, pattern and directory is here, so adding
one is a reviewable line in a policy file rather than an edit to a matcher.
`check:ci-tree-shape` is what enforces it, `.ci/config/tree-shape-baseline.json`
freezes what was already there on the day it landed, and that baseline is
SHRINK-ONLY as a SET.
SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY TWO TREES, not the whole repository. The root and
`agent/` are where a stray file is invisible: `packages/` and `docs/` are
reviewed as code and content, while a `.jsonl` at the root reaches nobody's
eye until a gate enumerates it. Widening the scope is a separate decision with
its own baseline, not a tightening of this one.
THE AGENT DIRECTORY CLASSES ARE CHECKED AGAINST THE HOOK, NOT COPIED FROM IT.
`wl_store.AGENT_RESERVED_DIRS` already names every directory under `agent/`
that is not a session, and the gate asserts SET EQUALITY between that frozenset
and the `agent_dirs` classes below, in both directions. That is the point of
the derivation: when the hook learns a directory and this file does not, the
gate says so instead of the two quietly describing different trees. The set was
already stale when this landed -- `pr` and `legacy` were missing from the hook
and had been reported as phantom peer sessions.
A CLASS IS A PERMISSION, NOT A REQUIREMENT. Nothing here says a file must
exist; every entry says a file matching it is allowed to. An absent permitted
file is a matter for whatever gate owns it.

root_files.why: Depth-1 files at the repository root. Every one is a toolchain manifest, a config a tool discovers by walking up, an entry point a human types, or a document a reader opens first.

root_dirs.why: Depth-1 directories at the repository root. A new one is a new top-level concept and is worth a line here.

agent_files.why: Depth-1 files directly under agent/. A plan is matched by its own pattern below, because which FOLDER a given plan belongs in is plan_lifecycle's business rather than this file's.

patterns.why: The STUB namespace, and nothing else since S5 of agent/plans/PLAN-agent-tree-lifecycle.md: every plan moved into agent/plans/ and left a one-line pointer here, and check:ci-plan-folders F1 refuses a real plan at this depth.

agent_dirs.why: Every directory under agent/ that is NOT a session. This list is asserted equal to wl_store.AGENT_RESERVED_DIRS in both directions; see the comment above.

classes.name: archive
classes.why: Frozen history, moved here when work concludes. Append-only; check:ci-plan-boxes G-A2 enforces that.

classes.name: programs
classes.why: Handoff program suites, one directory per slug.

classes.name: worklist
classes.why: The append-only worklist event log, one JSONL per session prefix. The path is the Stop hook's contract and does not move.

classes.name: reggate
classes.why: The per-branch effort-cap ledger, agent/reggate/<branch>.jsonl. The path is the hook's contract and does not move.

classes.name: plans
classes.why: Where a plan lives: active and backlog at the top, _done/ and _removed/ beneath. check:ci-plan-folders owns everything inside it.

classes.name: ledgers
classes.why: Append-only measurement logs a gate writes and reads back, agent/ledgers/census-*.jsonl. A .jsonl at the top of a directory of documents reaches nobody's eye, which is the class this whole file exists for.

classes.name: legacy
classes.why: Pre-per-session notes kept as a record. Frozen.

agent_session_dirs.why: A session's own notes. The name is the sanitised 8-character slug wl_store.agent_session_slug mints, which tells a session directory from a reserved one by SHAPE rather than by list.

bare_relative_scan.why: A module that builds a repository path out of a bare relative string answers the CALLER's working directory, not the tree. That is how a second reggate ledger appeared under .claude/hooks/stop/agent/, and how the standing-orders brief reported 0 plan files when run from a subdirectory.
bare_relative_scan.why_derived: The first path segment is compared against the repository's own top-level directory names, taken from git rather than typed here, so the rule cannot go stale as the tree grows.
bare_relative_scan.why_reached: REACHED, not merely built. A relative constant a caller always joins to a root it was given is the CORRECT pattern; the defect is a literal the filesystem is touched through. So `open`, `os.listdir` and `os.scandir` are findings on sight, and a `Path(...)` literal is one only when a filesystem method is called on it in the same expression.
